appearance.bark_look.thickness.note: The genus's bark thickness as its reference species', prunus-emarginata (plantgen-claude project-files/bark/records/prunus-emarginata.json): text: about 1/4 in (Sargent) as the cap; FOFEM 0.062 doubted

appearance.bark_look.stages.twig.note: The genus's twig stage as its reference species, prunus-emarginata, shows it (plantgen-claude project-files/bark/records/prunus-emarginata.json): stage: text: 'bright red, conspicuously marked by large pale lenticels in their second season' (Sargent)

appearance.bark_look.stages.trunk.note: The genus's trunk stage as its reference species, prunus-emarginata, shows it (plantgen-claude project-files/bark/records/prunus-emarginata.json): stage: text: 'smooth dark brown surface marked by horizontal light gray interrupted bands and by rows of oblong orange-colored lenticels' (Sargent); 'break and curl cross-wise' (VT, search excerpt). Bands drawn as mottle until a banding layer exists

traits.short_shoots.note: Kaplan, pp. 314-315: in Prunus the long-shoot leaves fall and short shoots arise in their axils on older wood, bearing clusters of leaves and flowers.

traits.fruit_type.note: Wikipedia, Prunus (read 2026-10-17): the fruit is a fleshy drupe around one large hard-shelled seed. Stated here so the genus does not take Rosaceae's aggregate fruit.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 genus aggregate for Prunus (gwddagg_v2.2_genus.csv, read): specific gravity 0.6 (wsg_est, the hierarchical-model genus mean, from 320 records in 70 sources); trunks 0.61, branches 0.6. A species with its own measurements states its own. Basic density is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

traits.note: Jepson's Manual of the Flowering Plants of California (1925), read in full: calyx 5-cleft; petals spreading; stamens 15 to 30; pistil 1, style terminal (tribe Drupeae, ovary superior).
